493: 1. Not to marry a woman—no distinction whether obligatory marriage or not; the custom in our region is uniform. Remarrying a divorcee is permitted as it's not such a joyous occasion.
2. Because at that time—it's not appropriate to increase joy. Nevertheless, if something requiring Shehecheyanu arises, one may recite it.

3. It's fine—lest another precede him. Also permitted to make an engagement feast. Now that betrothal occurs only at the wedding itself, still permitted to arrange matches and make a feast, but dancing is forbidden, and certainly other voluntary dancing.
4. They don't punish him—specifically for marriage where he performed a mitzvah. But if he cut hair during the Omer, they would fine and punish him.

5. Everything is permitted—for those who cut hair from Lag BaOmer onward. But for us who prohibit haircutting (§63), marriage is also forbidden, as marriage and haircutting share the same law. Conversely, our custom permits marriage and haircutting until Rosh Chodesh Iyar. If Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbat, permitted to cut hair Friday for Shabbat's honor and marry that day since the main feast will be on Shabbat.
6. Until Lag BaOmer—inclusive, meaning 33 complete days. Day 34 is strict only at night; once sunrise comes it's permitted, as part of the day counts as the whole.
7. They say then they stopped—though also on day 34 some died, the main cessation was on day 33.
8. On day 33—holds that on day 33 they completely stopped dying.
9. Tachanun not recited—also on the eve of the 32nd.
10. Until 33 itself—after sunrise, as part of the day is like the whole.

11. Not from evening—some later authorities permit haircutting from evening. For marriage, leniency only on Lag BaOmer day itself. However, when Lag BaOmer falls Friday and there's hardship, may permit the night before.
12. Ba'al Brit—the sandek, mohel, and father of the boy even if not circumcising himself (Rema: "or circumcised his son" means has a son needing circumcision). But not the escorts.
13. To cut hair during Sefirah—even the day before circumcision near evening before going to synagogue. If circumcision falls on Shabbat, permitted Friday even before noon.

14. Some practice… and it's an error—all agree on prohibiting 33 days but with different customs. Some from the second day of Pesach until Lag BaOmer. Some subtract the first 16 days until the second of Rosh Chodesh Iyar, then prohibit until Shavuot. One who holds both leniencies (Rosh Chodesh Iyar and from Lag BaOmer onward) errs.

15. They should not cut hair from Lag BaOmer onward—until Shavuot itself. In our region, the custom is to marry and cut hair during the three boundary days. Must complete 33 days of mourning observance. In Vilna: prohibit from first of Rosh Chodesh Iyar until 3 Sivan morning except Lag BaOmer. Each follows local custom.
16. Part of this custom—some people practice one way, some another.

17. Leniency in both—adopting leniency until Rosh Chodesh Iyar and from Lag BaOmer onward is contradictory. May adopt stringencies (prohibit Pesach to Shavuot except Lag BaOmer). If local custom is known, don't deviate.
